title: Auto-approve small, low-risk refunds
summary: Refunds under $50 from low-risk customers are now approved and paid on the spot instead of waiting for finance. Everything else still goes to a person, now with a risk score attached. The Slack ping and the nightly receipt job are gone: receipts are emailed the moment money moves.
riskNote: Money now leaves without a human check for small refunds, so the $50 limit, the risk threshold, and the fail-closed path all need testing.

nodes.title: Risk check
nodes.sub: Asks how risky this customer is

detail.headline: New: every refund gets a fraud score before anything else happens.
detail.summary: Before deciding, the refund service asks the RiskScore service for a score from 0 (safe) to 100 (risky). If the service is slow or down, the customer is treated as risky, so the refund goes to a person rather than being paid automatically.
detail.after: Scores the customer in under 0.8 seconds, or gives up and treats them as risky.

detail.riskNote: Adds a network call to every refund request. It fails closed, which is the safe direction.

patch: +// Fraud score from 0 (safe) to 100 (risky). Fails closed: if the service is down,
+// the customer is treated as risky so a person looks at the refund.

detail.headline: New decision: is it under $50, low risk, and the first refund this month?
detail.summary: This is the rule that lets money go out without a person. All three must be true: the amount is under $50, the risk score is below 30, and the customer has had no other refund in the last 30 days.

qa.check: Refund of $49.99, score 10, no recent refunds

qa: A refund in another currency is compared in cents of that currency (check this is intended)
detail.riskNote: This decides when money is paid without a human. Off-by-one mistakes at $50 or score 30 cost real money.
detail.uncertain: The amount is compared in cents of the order’s own currency. The code doesn’t convert currencies, so “$50” means 50 units of whatever currency the order used.
